recentItems.title: Chinese film director Wen Muye on food, war and longing for peace
recentItems.description:
"Once Upon a Time in the Middle East" is one of China's top-grossing films this summer. It follows a Chinese restaurateur whose life is upended when war erupts around him. Ahead of its international debut this September, director Wen Muye spoke to CGTN about what inspired the film – and the message he hopes it carries beyond China.

recentItems.title: US teacher Sakolsky leaves 'a part of my heart' in China
recentItems.description:
Retired US teacher Ronald Sakolsky, who donated thousands of dollars to plant trees in China, has returned home after a visit that left him deeply moved.

In an interview, he said the trip was a chance to reunite with old Chinese friends, including Yin Yuzhen, the activist who planted a forest in the Mu Us desert sands.

"The earth is alive because of Mrs. Yin Yuzhen," Sakolsky said, proud of his friend.

He also praised China's "beautiful" cities, saying the country felt as if it had already entered the 22nd century.

He was struck by the pace of development but also by how traditions remain deeply rooted in society – even as the skyline grows taller. "I've left a part of my heart in China," Sakolsky said, his voice catching.

recentItems.title: Expert: GGI empowers world's majority against unilateralism
recentItems.description:
Alexander Bobrov, head of the Diplomatic Studies Division at the Institute for Strategic Studies and Forecasts of the Peoples' Friendship University of Russia, says Russian diplomacy now regards the United States and its allies as a "global minority" and increasingly views their unilateral actions as unjust. The Global Governance Initiative (GGI) seeks to empower the "world's majority" by advancing a more democratic world order in the 21st century and supporting organizations such as BRICS and the UN.

recentItems.title: Expert: China champions global governance reform
recentItems.description:
Is the current global governance system outdated? Sudheendra Kulkarni, an aide to former Indian Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee, says Western countries represent only 15% of the world's population but still dominate international decision-making. He says China is a key supporter of democratizing this system. Through its Global Governance, Development and Security Initiatives, it seeks to establish a fairer and multipolar approach that empowers the global 85%, he noted.

recentItems.title: Where does a story begin? #factstell
recentItems.description:
Most viewers catch a news story mid-action – at the moment tensions snap or accusations fly. In this episode of Facts Tell, we examine the December 2025 encounter between Chinese and Japanese military aircraft east of the Miyako Strait. Japan focused on alleged radar illumination by a Chinese J-15 fighter, while China said its Liaoning aircraft carrier group was conducting pre-announced training and that Japanese aircraft repeatedly interefered by entering the exercise area. Where a story begins matters. A radar-lock claim suggests sudden escalation. A response to interference tells a very different story. 
#factstell

recentItems.title: What's next in China-US relations, top-level diplomacy
recentItems.description:
Chinese Premier Li Qiang met with a delegation from the US-China Business Council in Beijing earlier this week, stressing that China will address the reasonable concerns of US companies and ensure a level playing field under the law. Last week, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi also met with US Ambassador to China David Perdue, calling on both sides to implement the important consensus reached by their presidents, remove disruptions, and clear obstacles to high-level exchanges. Where do China-US relations go from here, before the next round of top-level diplomacy? CGTN's Tian Wei spoke with Sean Stein, the president of the US-China Business Council, who's a close observer and active participant in the relationship for decades. What can both sides do now to turn a framework of constructive engagement and strategic stability into reality? Here's that conversation.
